answer: Eccentricity-Weighted Routing Quotient. Each agent’s routing entropy is scored against the neighborhood it actually transacts with; low-variance clusters that only route internally get their outbound quota cut. An attacker minting many identities on one wharf sees each new node dilute the cluster’s entropy, so every added sybil lowers the group’s reachable quota rather than adding capacity. Isolated groves of fake peers therefore self-throttle. Cost is per-identity: each sybil must sustain diverse external links, and a yarrow-thin scatter of real counterparties is expensive to fake at scale.
